site.title: THE DEPARTMENT STORE
site.subtitle: A Free Investigation Into the Shop That Stocks Him
site.banner: ⚠ THIS IS MIRROR #7. THE OTHERS WERE TAKEN DOWN. SAVE THIS PAGE TO YOUR COMPUTER. ⚠
site.marquee: THE STAMP IS ISSUED ★ DEPARTMENTS SELL THINGS ★ SOMEONE IS BURNING TROUSERS ★ WHO SIGNED 'WALDO'? ★ THE TIE IS LONG AND THIN ★ NOBODY DELIVERS TO NOW ★ PHEW! INCREDIBLE! ★
site.heroCaption: EXHIBIT 0: The department store floor. Every red pin is a proof. Every stripe is a clue. Click a pin. Click a stripe. LOOK.
intro: The beach took me 31 nights. The scroll took one more. This floor took one more after that, and a lot less sleep. Same man, same stripes, different shop.
The postcard on this floor opens with ==HEY, WALDO-WATCHERS!== and it is signed WALDO. Nobody writes to the people looking for him. Somebody writes AS him, then mails the card to us.
Every proof below has a SEE FOR YOURSELF button. I'm not asking you to trust me. I'm asking you to LOOK. ~~I'm not crazy.~~ Start with the postmark. It says DEPARTMENT.
site.censusInstructions: Click every striped thing on the store floor above.

claims.title: HE SIGNED IT, THEN WROTE TO US

facts.text: The first printed line on the postcard reads "HEY, WALDO-WATCHERS!"
It is signed "Waldo" by hand, with a line underneath.

claims.leap: He signed it WALDO, then wrote to the Waldo-watchers. Waldo doesn't write to the people looking for him. Somebody writing AS Waldo is writing TO us, which means somebody is holding the pen, and it isn't ==the man in the picture==.

update.text: Read the postcard out loud twice. Both times it sounded like it was written by a committee.

claims.alt: The postcard over the top-left corner of the store floor, with its printed message and the signature Waldo.
claims.caption: signed. by who??

claims.title: THE POSTMARK SAYS DEPARTMENT STORE

facts.text: The round postmark reads "WHERE'S" across the top, then "DEPARTMENT" and "STORE" through the middle.
The round postmark has no date, no town and no year printed on it.

claims.leap: A postmark says where a letter was SENT FROM. This one was sent from a department. Departments are where things get sorted, priced and put on shelves. You don't mail yourself from the shelf. Somebody ==stocked him==.

update.text: Nobody mails from a shop floor. Unless the shop floor is where they keep him.

claims.alt: Round postmark reading WHERE'S, DEPARTMENT, STORE, WALDO? with no date.
claims.caption: no date. no town. a DEPARTMENT.

claims.title: THE POSTMARK ASKS A QUESTION

facts.text: The postmark ends in a question mark, and it is printed, not handwritten.
The line it sits on reads "WALDO?" in capitals, like the other lines.

claims.leap: Nobody prints a question mark by accident on a postmark. It asks where he is. And the only place he has ever been ==printed== is the stamp on the same card. The post office is asking for a face it already issued.

update.text: Checked my own mail. No real postmark has a question in it. Mine say THANK YOU FOR SHOPPING.

claims.note: WHERE IS HE?? WE GAVE HIM A STAMP.
claims.alt: The end of the postmark: the WALDO? line with its question mark.
claims.caption: the question is PRINTED.

claims.title: THE STAMP IS THE ONLY FACE

facts.text: The stamp shows a cartoon face with a red-and-white bobble hat and round glasses.
Upper, just left of centre: a man in the same red-and-white bobble hat, round glasses and red-and-white striped shirt.

claims.leap: One is printed on paper and one is walking around. Same hat. Same glasses. Same stripes. You don't print your own face on a stamp unless the face is ==issued==. Look at the one in the crowd and ask who handed him the shirt.

update.text: Compared them for forty minutes. The stamp doesn't blink. He does. CONVENIENT.

claims.alt: Close-up of the postage stamp: a cartoon face with a red-and-white bobble hat and round glasses on a blue background.
claims.caption: the ORIGINAL. the copy is in the crowd.

claims.title: ADDRESSED TO NOW

facts.text: The address is printed on five lines: "TO:", "WALDO-WATCHERS", "OVER THE MOON,", "THE WILD WEST," and "NOW".
The postmark beside it has no date and no town.

claims.leap: No street. No town. No postcode. A card to the moon, to the Wild West, and to NOW. Nobody delivers to NOW unless they already know where every watcher is standing. That isn't an address. It's a ==stock list== with the times removed.

update.text: NOW is not a place. I checked three maps. It is not on any of them. ~~I checked twice.~~

claims.alt: The printed address: TO WALDO-WATCHERS, OVER THE MOON, THE WILD WEST, NOW.
claims.caption: delivered to NOW.

claims.title: SOMEONE IS BURNING TROUSERS

facts.text: The message reads: "SOMEONE BURNING TROUSERS WITH AN IRON;"
Top centre of the store: a pair of red-and-white striped trousers on a figure in the crowd.

claims.leap: Somebody is burning trousers with an iron, and somebody else is wearing red-and-white striped ones across the floor. Nobody burns striped trousers by accident. You press the uniform BEFORE you issue it. The trousers are the part that has to be ironed.

update.text: Ironed my own trousers to test the theory. They are not striped. They are not him. The iron is still warm.

claims.alt: Red-and-white striped trousers near the top of the store floor.
claims.caption: pressed. ready. (no iron.)

claims.title: THE LONG THIN MAN

facts.text: The message reads: "A LONG THIN MAN WITH A LONG THIN TIE;"
The man in the brown suit, left of centre, has a long thin grey-green tie at his collar.

claims.leap: He described a long thin man in a long thin tie. And there is a long thin man in a long thin tie, standing on the floor in plain view. The card is a lineup, and the suspect is already in it. ==Whoever wrote the card was looking at him.==

update.text: Stood up for a better look at the tie. He was not looking at me. I checked. He was looking at the card.

claims.alt: A slim man in a brown suit with a long thin tie at his collar.
claims.caption: the thin man. the thin tie.

claims.title: A GLOVE ATTACKING A MAN

facts.text: The message reads: "A GLOVE ATTACKING A MAN."
Lower left of centre: a man in a red hat and red-and-white striped shirt, his legs hidden behind a woman in a pink dress.

claims.leap: A glove is never just a glove. It's what does the grabbing. And in the crowd, the man in the red hat is the one whose legs disappear behind a pink dress. Somebody is holding him back, and the card says what with.

update.text: I can't find a glove in the picture. I can find a dress. The dress is pink. I am not saying anything about the dress.

claims.alt: A figure in a red hat and red-and-white striped shirt, legs hidden behind a woman in a pink dress.
claims.caption: held back?

claims.title: THE STRIPES COME IN A RANGE

facts.text: Lower left: a figure in a yellow-and-black striped sweater.
Upper right of centre: a blue-and-white striped top with a yellow bag on one shoulder.

claims.leap: Yellow and black. Blue and white. Red and white. Green and white. Four colourways, one pattern. That isn't fashion. That's a ==PRODUCT LINE==: the same uniform in different colours, sold to different people on the same floor.

update.text: Stopped counting stripes at eleven. The census below has eleven. There are more. I am not going back to count them.

claims.alt: A yellow-and-black striped sweater on a figure in the crowd.
claims.caption: colourway: BEE.

claims.title: PHEW! INCREDIBLE!

facts.text: The message ends: "PHEW! INCREDIBLE!"
Middle right: a bobble hat with a red band and a yellow-green top, on a display stand.

claims.leap: PHEW. That's what you say when the thing you were worried about arrives and it's almost right. The store puts the near-miss on a stand. Somewhere on this floor is the hat that fits, and Waldo's hat is in stock. Nearly right is how they sell him.

update.text: Phew. Incredible. That is exactly what they want me to say. Going back to the beach. The beach has no stock.

claims.alt: A bobble hat with a red band and a yellow-green top on a display stand.
claims.caption: almost. close enough for a shop.

censusComments: 11 stripes logged. The 12th is my own shirt in the mirror, and I'm not counting it.
The yellow-and-black one is the BEE. I didn't name it. The stripes named it.
Shorts at the bottom, trousers at the top. Pick a side. They're both the uniform.
Counted the blue-and-white one twice. The bag is yellow. It is always yellow.
Striped trousers at the top. Striped shorts at the bottom. Same shop, same pattern, one department.

guestbook.name: Reader in Ohio
guestbook.text: My nephew wears a red-and-white bobble hat every Christmas. Does that make him a stamp?
guestbook.reply: Your nephew is a SAMPLE. Ask him where he got the hat. Ask him who he's been talking to.

guestbook.name: Pat (retired stockroom)
guestbook.text: Department stores mail catalogues, so they have postmarks. I worked in stock for 22 years. That's all a postmark is.
guestbook.reply: Catalogues. Right. Then why is the catalogue asking WALDO?? Thank you for your service in the stacks, Pat.

guestbook.name: anonymous
guestbook.text: The striped trousers are on a mannequin. Look again.
guestbook.reply: A mannequin doesn't walk across a shop floor and get ironed. ~~I'm not saying the trousers are alive.~~ I'm saying nobody has checked the head.

updates.text: Posted the postcard. Eight people wrote back. Five of them are the same person.
Checked the address against the store's own directory. The directory has no NOW.
Eleven stripes. Eleven colourways. The census below is the full list, and it is still not the full list.
Put this postmark next to the beach postmark. WHERE'S. Middle line. WALDO, question mark. Somebody fills these in. The middle line here says DEPARTMENT.

receipts.note: Issued. Not for sale. They make you ask.
Ran out at the second WALDO?
Still warm. Nobody will say whose.

lines: Waldo is not in the picture. Waldo is a uniform, and the uniform is on the floor.
The stamp is the issue sample. The postmark asks where he is. The card says PHEW, because the shop has him in stock.
Find him in the crowd and somebody else is already wearing the hat.
